- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp price spikes in history, then gradually decline — model overshoots and lags in correction.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to smoothly revert to historical mean after volatility spikes.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecasts often underestimate the magnitude of downward corrections following upward spikes.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — underestimates the speed of decline.
- When history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising or falling), model fails to align forecast direction with the trend’s persistence.
- Model overfits to recent high values, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in adjusting to true price movements, especially in the 15–25 day window.
- Model tends to overcorrect after sharp declines, creating artificial rebounds that don’t match true market behavior.
